correctness.rationale: For labelled K_{2m} minus a perfect matching, a selected vertex sees S minus its mate bit ones in exactly 2m-1 closed-neighborhood positions, giving an exact three-regime update law. The cut identity c=m^2-(S-m)^2-k and S congruent k modulo 2 classify every maximum cut. Explicit finite paths force entrance into that locus from any initial configuration; the even case consists of fixed points. For odd m, inclusion between middle subsets and two independent mixed-pair orientations gives one connected doubled-edge-subdivision transition graph. Each edge has transition probability 1/(2m), so reversibility, the block Laplacian, and the published middle-level graph eigenvalues prove the exact spectral gap. Two standalone direct-rule programs corroborate full recurrent SCCs for 2<=m<=7 (21,840 states) and spectra for m=3,5,7. No infinite claim rests on finite tests.

value.rationale: The object is a canonical graph family measuring the effect of deleting a perfect matching from a clique under a standard zero-temperature anti-coordination rule. An exact parity phase transition separates exponentially many absorbing recurrent classes from a single irreducible class. The odd-parameter chain is identified as a doubled-edge subdivision of an established middle-level graph, and its explicit relaxation spectral gap scales as m^{-2}. These structural and quantitative classifications provide more than a routine fixed-state count or table reproduction and motivate analysis of equilibration on nearly complete interaction networks.
